facts.fact: Caroline has suddenly brought a maid named Patricia, after a week of coming to the Bishop library alone.
Zane concludes Grey must have discovered Caroline was out by herself and put a stop to it.
facts.anchor: There was only one logical conclusion. Grey.

facts.fact: Zane calls her marriage like a lamb going to slaughter: Orson handsome outside, but a rotted soul underneath.
facts.anchor: Christ, I couldn’t believe this woman, this delicate and intelligent creature, had willingly married Orson Grey. It was like a lamb going to slaughter. What had she possibly seen in him? He was handsome, no one would deny it. But underneath was a rotted soul full of self-importance and selfishness.

facts.fact: Zane hits on a hunting trip as the way to get Orson out of New York.
facts.anchor: It hit me then with the force of a sledgehammer. Why hadn’t I thought of it sooner? “Hunting. A trip he can’t turn down.”

facts.fact: Zane dashes off a telegram to his investigator Cribbs to arrange the trip, covering all costs and allowing no women.
facts.anchor: “Fuck you.” I picked up my pen and dashed off a telegram to Cribbs. My investigator would know who organizes these sorts of trips and how to craft one appealing enough for Orson Grey. I handed the piece of paper to Fletcher. “Send this right away.”

facts.fact: Caroline says Orson hovered each morning as she left, and she dreads the day he forbids her to leave the house.
facts.anchor: Each morning, Orson hovered as I left, his scowl growing deeper and deeper. I knew it was only a matter of time before he decided my work was done and forbade me to leave the house. I dreaded it like an appointment with a tooth puller. I was jumpy around him, nerves stretched taut, as I waited for the metaphorical blade to fall.

facts.fact: Orson announces a hunting trip West to Wyoming for elk, away five or six weeks (35-42 days).
facts.anchor: “Now, don’t you worry. I won’t be away too long. Five or six weeks at most.”

facts.fact: Orson confines Caroline to the gardens, forbids her contact with Camilla and orders staff surveillance; she fears a doctor or an asylum.
facts.anchor: He studied my face for a long moment, his expression inscrutable. I couldn’t tell what he was thinking, but he concentrated intently, as if I were a puzzle he couldn’t solve. Finally, he let go of the door. “Fine. I won’t summon Dr. Baird. But I will instruct the staff to keep an eye on you. If you seem unwell, I want Dr. Baird sent for straightaway.”
